context:
Goal: builders and reviewers judge screens by one list.
Problem (rule): the house-rules record lists 14 ids, while the design docs hold 34 ux headings, and no check compares them.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/ux-house-rules.md:14-19 lists 14 ids as the house rules.
Based on (read): docs/design/principles.md has 27 ux headings and docs/design/layout.md has 7.
Based on (read): no lint or hook reads either list.
Departs from: main, with two lists that differ — makes one list and checks it.

All 34, each with its rule sentence:
The 14 the record lists:
- ux-label-once: A label or a status word shows once on a screen.
- ux-answer-at-press: The answer to a press shows where the press was.
- ux-long-run-stops: A run that takes more than a few seconds shows a Stop control.
- ux-all-is-well: A status summary names only what is not normal.
- ux-thumb-zone: On a phone layout, the main input and the main action sit in reach of the thumb.
- ux-works-when-script-fails: When JavaScript, WebGL or WebGPU is off or fails, the person still reaches the content and the main action, or a page that says what is missing and leads on.
- ux-lost-scene-recovers: When the GPU drops a 3D scene, the person sees words that say so, and the scene comes back when the GPU returns.
- ux-still-scene-draws-nothing: A 3D scene that does not move draws no frames, so it does not spend the person's battery.
- ux-canvas-has-words: A canvas or 3D view that carries information has a name and a text equivalent, and each act in it works from the keyboard.
- ux-scroll-stays-native: Scroll moves the page at the person's pace, so they can read and find their way.
- ux-forced-colors-hold: In forced-colors mode, such as a Windows contrast theme, each control, its edge, its focus ring and its state stay visible.
- ux-full-height-fits: A full-height region fits the visible phone screen, with the browser bars shown or hidden, so its bottom content and actions are never under the bars.
- ux-vitals-measured: Each changed route's Core Web Vitals meet the "good" lines on web.dev in a mobile lab trace and, where it exists, at the 75th percentile of field data.
- ux-feature-baseline-or-fallback: A web feature outside the repo's browser target runs only behind a feature test, with a fallback the person can use.

The other 20 (in the design docs only):
- ux-press-moves-nothing: A press, a load or a change of state moves no other content.
- ux-order-holds-still: A list keeps a plain, predictable order, and an act on a row does not re-rank the list.
- ux-unknown-is-not-empty: A screen shows loading, failed, unknown and loaded as different states.
- ux-statements-are-true: Screen copy claims only what the product does and what the owner confirmed.
- ux-machine-text-hidden: A code, a path, a record id or raw server text shows only in a closed disclosure.
- ux-no-dead-end: Each refusal, error and end page has a control on that screen that leads on: a fix, or another way such as a phone number.
- ux-empty-one-action: An empty state is one sentence that says what fills it, and one control that fills it.
- ux-ask-or-undo: A destructive press asks first when it cannot be undone, and acts and offers Undo when it can.
- ux-keep-what-was-made: Never discard input that a person made and that no server can return.
- ux-control-earns-place: A control that changes nothing on a view is absent, and an expected control that is off says why.
- ux-one-plain-name: Each screen and each act has one plain name, and each icon has one meaning.
- ux-a11y-floor: Each screen meets the accessibility floor in `a11y.md`.
- ux-haptics-feel-substantial: An app on a device with haptics considers a haptic on controls that change a value, such as sliders, steppers and toggles, so the change feels substantial.
- ux-gap-on-parent: The parent spaces its children.
- ux-layout-primitives: A page is built from a few named layout primitives.
- ux-control-beside-area: A control sits next to the area it changes.
- ux-component-reads-its-box: A shared component changes its shape from its own width, with a container query.
- ux-variant-extends-home: A screen that needs a shared component to look or act a little different extends the component.
- ux-fluid-tokens: Space and type that grow with the box use clamp() tokens.
- ux-swift-same-intent: A Swift screen follows the same four rules with its own tools.

lastAnswer.note: Asked: "i need to see them all to decide". Rewritten 22:30 CST: all 34 rules listed in the context, split 14 listed and 20 not.

options.gain: One list; every ux heading binds builders and reviewers.
options.how: The record cites the headings in principles.md and layout.md instead of listing ids. A check fails when a cited heading is missing.
options.label: All 34 are house rules
options.lose: 20 more rules bind every screen review.

options.gain: Fewer binding rules on each screen review.
options.how: Keep the record's list. Mark the other 20 headings as guidance, and add a check that the 14 exist as headings.
options.label: Only the 14
options.lose: Two kinds of ux heading for readers to tell apart.
